title: Derived PartialEq/Eq on HeaderDateTime is field-wise, not instant-wise: equal moments at different offsets compare unequal
description:
header_typed.rs:67-79 derives `PartialEq, Eq` on HeaderDateTime by field. The derived equality compares year/month/day/hour/minute/second/tz_before_gmt/tz_hour/tz_minute byte-for-byte.

That means two HeaderDateTime values representing the *same instant* in time at *different* offsets compare as not-equal:

    let a = HeaderDateTime { year: 2024, month: 1, day: 1, hour: 12, minute: 0, second: 0,
                             tz_before_gmt: false, tz_hour: 0, tz_minute: 0 };  // 12:00 UTC
    let b = HeaderDateTime { year: 2024, month: 1, day: 1, hour: 13, minute: 0, second: 0,
                             tz_before_gmt: false, tz_hour: 1, tz_minute: 0 };  // 13:00 +0100
    assert_ne!(a, b);   // but they are the same instant

Caller-facing consequence: a JMAP server normalising dates from disparate clients (some sending UTC, some sending +0100) will treat logically-identical timestamps as distinct values. Set/HashMap membership, dedup, and equality checks all silently misbehave.

The contract `parse_header_typed` documents (line 178) is "best-effort parse the RFC 5322 §3.3 date-time". RFC 5322 §3.3 explicitly states that a "+HHMM" or "-HHMM" offset is the difference from UTC — semantically equivalent moments. The Rust PartialEq derive does not reflect that semantics, and the doc does not warn callers.

Fix options:
- Document that PartialEq is field-wise (not instant-wise). Direct the caller to `to_timestamp()` for instant-equality.
- Drop the derive and write a hand-rolled PartialEq that compares `to_timestamp()` values. (Then `name: 2024 +0000` and `2024 +0100` are not-equal at the structural level — losing structural comparison.)
- Make HeaderDateTime opaque (no public fields) and require `to_timestamp()`/component accessors. Callers can no longer derive their own meaningful equality.

This is distinct from MIME-o2c.9 (constructable without validation) and MIME-o2c.10 (mirrors mail_parser::DateTime). It is about *behavior of the trait derive*, not field validity or upstream mirroring.

Line refs:
- header_typed.rs:67  `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]`
- header_typed.rs:75-78 `tz_before_gmt`, `tz_hour`, `tz_minute` — fields that participate in derived Eq.
close_reason: Documentation batch on the typed header surface: (.7) parse_header_typed now states trailing CRLF is permitted-but-not-required (matching the implementation); (.8) EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name field docs now state the trim+empty-to-None normalization; (.12) HeaderValueTyped doc has a Serde Wire Format section pinning the current externally-tagged shape and explicitly distinguishing it from RFC 8621 wire format (callers responsible for that mapping); (.17) parse_header_typed doc now carries one runnable example per HeaderForm variant (six total); (.24) HeaderDateTime has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is field-wise not instant-wise, with a worked example and the to_timestamp escape hatch; (.25) EmailAddress has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is byte-exact (no RFC 5321 domain case-folding) and pointing callers at manual canonicalisation; (.30) parse_header_typed doc has an Empty-Result Ambiguity table making explicit that callers cannot distinguish malformed-vs-empty-vs-non-UTF-8 and flagging the future-direction (strict variant / warnings tuple). No code changes.
